newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast spot power steady on humid weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast spot power steady on humid weather.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. on Wednesday ended steady versus Tuesday's values on warm, humid conditions in the southern parts of the region, market sources said.
Rain combined with warm temperatures in much of Florida, and lower portions of Alabama and Georgia helped support air-conditioning demand, traders said.
"It's hot and steamy...It's pretty healthy load," said a Florida trader.
Today's forecasts showed temperatures in the southern half of the Southeast topping in the mid-80's to 90 Fahrenheit degrees and bottoming in the mid-60's to mid-70's.
The latest extended weather reports indicated that most of the Southeast would receive cooler to much cooler-than-normal autumn weather.

In the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC), peak, firm electricity during heavy load hours on Thursday for delivery into the northern part of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) distribution system was assessed at $14.00-$15.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), unchanged from Tuesday's quote for Wednesday power.
Firm, off-peak power prices for Thursday was valued at near $12.00, also unchanged from Tuesday's level.
At the Georgia-Florida border, firm electricity for during a 12-hour peak on Thursday was discussed at $22.00-$23.00 per MWh, flat from Tuesday's range.
Firm, off-peak power prices at the Ga./Fla. border were again pegged at $16.00-$17.00.
TVA was heard offering peak, non-firm electricity for Thursday at $19.00 a MWh, up from Tuesday's $17.50.

Florida Power Corp's 825 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 3 nuclear unit in Red Level, Fla., and Duke Power Co's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear station in Seneca, S.C., remained off line, with no restart dates set.
